info.title: py1815 master
info.summary: A DNP3 master for exercising outstations, as a service.
info.description:
Every operation of the master, each as a route that takes its parameters as a JSON object and answers with a JSON object.

An outstation that does not answer is not an error: the exchange's `outcome` is `timeout`. An answer has `ok: false` only when the message could not be acted on, or there was no connection to ask over.

The service listens on the machine it runs on unless it was given a token, which every request then carries as `Authorization: Bearer`, or as a `token` query parameter where a header cannot be set.

post.description: In engineering units, with each point's quality. A point is named by its address, as in `AI148`, or by its name or the name's first sentence; a name the tables give to more than one point is refused with the addresses it could mean. A group is a function, by key, name or purpose, or everything of one purpose, as in `Nameplate` or `Monitoring`. One request, unless the outstation refuses it whole for a range it does not serve: then each range is read again on its own, and a point no read returned is `not_reported`. The outstation has to have been given a profile: `--profile`, or `profile` in its configuration.

post.description: One request, in the order given. An analog value is divided by the point's multiplier and sent as the nearest whole number; one outside the point's range is refused before anything is sent. With `verify`, the input that mirrors each output is read afterwards and compared with what was asked, within one step of the multiplier. Refused as `not_allowed` unless the service was started to command. Sent once: a write whose answer did not arrive is reported as not known, and never sent again. The outstation has to have been given a profile: `--profile`, or `profile` in its configuration.

post.description: Three writes, in the order IEEE 1815.2 clause 6.1.3 lays the curve block out: the selector; the type, the number of points and the units of X and Y; then X and Y of each point. Each is made only when the one before it was accepted. The curve is then read back whatever happened. Values travel as the whole numbers given, since the units the curve declares say how they scale. Refused as `not_allowed` unless the service was started to command. Sent once: a write whose answer did not arrive is reported as not known, and never sent again. The outstation has to have been given a profile: `--profile`, or `profile` in its configuration.

post.description: Reads class 0, then output status, then every declared point neither returned. A declared point no read returned is absent; a point returned that is not declared is undeclared; a served point a class 0 read does or does not carry, against what is declared, is listed under `class_0`. A point's event class and deadband cannot be read from an outstation, so they are given as declared. Needs no profile.

get.summary: What happens unasked, as server-sent events
get.description: A stream that stays open. Each event's data is a JSON object with an `event` field: `frame`, `exchange`, `unsolicited`, `connection` or `outstations`, and the `outstation` it is about.

200.description: The stream.

401.description: A token is required, and is missing or wrong.

403.description: The request comes from another site, or names a host this server is not.

PointType.description: Binary input, binary output status, counter, frozen counter, analog input, analog output status.

startup.description: On connecting, and when the outstation reports that it restarted: stop its unsolicited reporting, then read everything it holds.

clear_restart.description: Clear the restart indication once it has been seen. A write: off in a service that was not started to command.

write_time.description: Set the outstation's clock when it asks for the time. A write: off in a service that was not started to command.

enable_unsolicited.description: After startup, ask the outstation to report these event classes without being polled.

events_when_indicated.description: Fetch events when a response says there are some waiting.

integrity_on_overflow.description: Read everything again when the outstation says its event buffer overflowed.

Tasks.description: What the master does for an outstation without being asked.

indications.description: The internal indications of the last response, by name.

counts.description: How the exchanges so far ended, by outcome.

points.description: Points reported so far, by type.

repeat.description: The scans being repeated, by kind, as seconds between them.

tasks_due.description: The tasks waiting to be done, in the order they will be.

reconnect.description: Seconds between attempts to make again a connection that was lost, or null when it is not made again.

profile.description: Points in the profile the outstation is meant to serve, by type, or null when no profile was given.

device_profile.description: Whether the outstation was given a Device Profile document for `der.compare`.

value.description: A state, a count or an analog value. A float with no number is sent as the string "NaN", "Infinity" or "-Infinity".

flags.description: The flag bits that are set, by name. Null for a variation that carries no flag octet, which is not the same as none being set.

oneOf.description: The time the outstation gave, in milliseconds since the epoch.

Object.description: One object out of a response, decoded.

value.description: An analog output's value as sent, or a binary output's control code.

status.description: The status the outstation answered with, by name, as in SUCCESS or NOT_SUPPORTED. Null if the response did not carry this control.

echoed.description: Whether what came back was the control as sent, apart from its status.

ControlStatus.description: What an outstation said about one control.

operated.description: Whether a request that operates was sent. False for a select the outstation refused, after which no operate is sent.

accepted.description: Whether the outstation accepted every control. Null when it never said: the request takes no acknowledgment, or the response did not arrive. That is not a refusal, and the output may have been operated.

exchanges.description: Each request made, in order: one, or a select and an operate.

Operated.description: A control request, or the two of a select and operate, and what came of them.

task.description: The task the master made the request for of its own accord, or null for a request that was asked for.

outcome.description: How the exchange ended. An outstation that did not answer is a timeout, and not an error.

indications.description: The internal indications of the last fragment, by name, or null if nothing arrived.

object_count.description: Objects received. More than are described in `objects` when a response is very large.

undecoded.description: Where an object could not be read: why, and the octets from there on.

Exchange.description: One request and everything that came back for it.

value.description: A state, a count or an analog value. A float with no number is sent as the string "NaN", "Infinity" or "-Infinity".

flags.description: The flag bits that are set, by name. Null for a variation that carries no flag octet, which is not the same as none being set.

PointValue.description: The last thing an outstation said about one point.

name.description: The name as the profile's tables have it.

label.description: The name without the values it lists, for a point that is an enumeration; otherwise the name.

enumeration.description: The values the point's name lists, in the order listed, or null when it lists none. A value is a number, a range such as `11-255`, or a number and up such as `99+`.

ProfilePoint.description: One point of the profile an outstation is meant to serve.

id.description: Counts up for the life of the trace.

direction.description: Sent by this master, or received.

oneOf.description: The transport header, on user data.
The application fragment, on the frame that completed it.

summary.description: One line that says what it is.

name.description: The name as the profile's tables have it.

label.description: The first sentence of the name, without the values it lists.

multiplier.description: The transmitted number times this is the engineering value.

states.description: A binary point's two states by name: 0, then 1.

mirror.description: The input that reads an output back, by address.

DerPoint.description: One point of the DER profile.

value.description: In engineering units: the transmitted number through the point's multiplier, or a state. Null when the point was not reported.

state.description: A binary point's state, by the name the tables give it.

flags.description: The flag bits that are set, by name. Null for a variation that carries no flag octet, which is not the same as none being set.

quality.description: What the flags say: `good` is ONLINE. `offline` is a value sent without ONLINE, which is how a disabled function's inputs travel. `not_reported` is a point the outstation did not return.

DerReading.description: One point of the DER profile, as the outstation reported it.

key.description: Its name in lower case, as in `volt-var`.

purpose.description: What the tables say it is for.

enable.description: The binary output that enables it.

status.description: The binary input that reports whether it is enabled.

supports.description: The binary input that says whether it is supported.

supported.description: What the outstation says. Null when it did not report it.

enabled.description: What the outstation says. Null when it did not report it.

curve_settings.description: The settings that name a curve by its number.

DerFunction.description: One DER function, and what the outstation says of it.

items.description: A state, a count or an analog value. A float with no number is sent as the string "NaN", "Infinity" or "-Infinity".

points.description: X and Y of each point, as transmitted: the units the curve declares say how to scale them.

referenced.description: Whether a function names this curve, where the outstation says.

Curve.description: The curve the curve block shows, as the outstation reported it.

event_class.description: The class its events are reported in, 0 for none, as declared.

class_0.description: Whether a class 0 read carries it, as declared.

Declared.description: One point as a Device Profile document declares it.

enabled.description: Whether the outstation says the function is enabled, read afterwards. Null when it did not say.

DerSwitched.description: A DER function enabled or disabled, and what its status input then said.

ExchangeSummary.description: One request, and how it ended, without its objects.

kind.description: `request`: the message could not be acted on. `connection`: there was no connection to ask over.

id.description: The id of the message, when it had one.

token.description: Required only when the service was started with a token.
